name: Ransomware group Blacksuit steals data from US branch of Swiss pharmaceutical company, Octapharma, on 17 April 2024
description:
Octapharma Plasma, the US branch of Octapharma, a Swiss pharmaceutical company involved in "protein manufacturing," or the manufacturing of plasma-dependent medical therapies, was hit by a ransomware attack by Blacksuit ransomware group on 17 April 2024. 
According to Octapharma's press release on 19 April, the company detected "suspicious activity" on its networks, which resulted in the company having to take its systems offline while an investigation was initiated; this impacted operations of over 100 plasma donation centres in the US. Days later, on 24 April 2024, the Blacksuit ransomware gang listed Octapharma Plasma on its leak site along with details about the attack. While the company was listed on the site, no data had been leaked; according to the group, data stolen included information on employees and clients, including medical examination information, employee contract information, and donor centre/lab data, as well as Social Security numbers of donors.
source_disclosure: Incident disclosed by media (without further information on source)
intelligence_impact: Data corruption (deletion/altering) but no leaking of data, no data breach/exfiltration OR major data breach / exfiltration, but no data corruption and/or leaking of data

name: Akira Ransomware Group Attacked the US Louisiana Special School District with Ransomware in May 2024
description: In June 2024, the Louisiana Special School District fell victim to a ransomware attack by the group Akira, resulting in a data breach that exposed personal and limited health information of students and staff, including national insurance numbers and addresses. The intrusion was discovered on 24 May and affected multiple departments, including the Office of Human Resources and the Louisiana School for the Deaf. Upon discovery, the district notified the Louisiana State Police and remediated the network security vulnerabilities. Affected individuals were notified beginning on 8 July, and the district expects to have data fully restored by 1 August.
intelligence_impact: Minor data breach/exfiltration (no critical/sensitive information), but no data corruption (deletion/altering) or leaking of data

name: Black Basta Ransomware Group Claims To Have Stolen 730 GB Of Data From American Oil Distributor 'Atlas Oil' In May 2024
description:
The Black Basta ransomware group claimed to have stolen 730GB of data from Atlas Oil, one of the largest distributors of fuel in the United States, on 20 May 2024.
According to samples of the stolen data that were leaked as proof of the data theft, the data could include corporate data, payroll information, employee and user IDs, and more. As of 22 May 2024, Atlas Oil had not confirmed the theft of data.
intelligence_impact: Minor data breach/exfiltration (no critical/sensitive information), data corruption (deletion/altering) and/or leaking of data

name: The LockBit ransomware group stole data and personal information of some customers from Evolve Bank & Trust
description:
The LockBit ransomware group stole data and personal information of some customers from Evolve Bank & Trust, the technology security company HackManac reported on social media on 23 June 2024.
The LockBit ransomware group first claimed to have hacked and stolen information from the Federal Reserve on 23 June 2024. This proved to be false when HackManac made the connection to Evolve Bank & Trust, and the bank admitted the incident the following day without referring to LockBit, but only to a cybercriminal organisation.
The stolen data included data and personal information of some Evolve retail bank customers and financial technology partners’ customers. The incident does not appear to have impacted banking customers’ debit cards and online and digital banking credentials. The attack compromised personal information of over 7.6 million individuals.
On 25 June, Affirm Holdings Inc. reported that its customer data could also be affected by the ransomware attack. Because the company [Affirm Holdings, Inc] shares the personal data of Affirm card users with Evolve to facilitate the issuance and management of Affirm cards, it is possible that the data of Affirm payment cardholders could also be exposed.
intelligence_impact: Minor data breach/exfiltration (no critical/sensitive information), data corruption (deletion/altering) and/or leaking of data

name: LockBit allegedly compromised Hawaiian Malama I Ke Ola Health Center with ransomware since mid-May 2024
description:
The LockBit ransomware group has allegedly compromised the systems of Malama I Ke Ola Health Center in Hawaii with ransomware since mid-May 2024. The attack disrupted normal service for two weeks. 
According to the Indian cybersecurity company FalconFeeds, LockBit claimed responsibility for the attack in its dark web forum.
The health center has not confirmed the ransomware attack officially yet.
On 26 September 2024, the Hawaiian Malama I Ke Ola Health Center filed a report with the Maine Attorney General's Office and published a statement on its website. It stated that an investigation revealed that unknown hackers gained unauthorised access to the network of the health centre in question from 4 to 7 May and that personal data may have been stolen. This included first and last names with one or more of the following identifiers: Social Security Number, Date Of Birth, Driver's License Number / State Id Number, Passport Number, Financial Account Number, Routing Number, Bank Name, Credit / Debit Card Number, Card CVV Expiration Date, Pin/Security Code, Login Information, Medical Diagnosis, Clinical Information, Medical Treatment/Procedure Information, Treatment Type, Treatment Location, Treatment Cost Information, Doctor's Name, Medical Record Number, Patient Account Number, Prescription Information and/ or Biometric Data.
intelligence_impact: No data breach/exfiltration or data corruption (deletion/altering) and/or leaking of data

name: LockBit Group targeted Systems of the City of Wichita, Kansas and Deploys Encryption Malware on 5 May 2024
description:
On 5 May 2024, an unknown threat actor used encryption malware to lock selected systems of the US City of Wichita, Kansas, resulting in the shutdown of certain computer networks and systems. 
On 7 May 2024, the ransomware group Lockbit claimed responsibility for the attack and added the city of Wichita to its extortion portal noting that it had exfiltrated information from compromised systems. LockBit threatened to release the stolen data if the demanded ransom was not paid by 15 May 2024.
intelligence_impact: Minor data breach/exfiltration (no critical/sensitive information), but no data corruption (deletion/altering) or leaking of data

name: RansomHub Ransomware Group Claims To Have Hit The US-American Pharmarcy Chain Rite Aid With Ransomware Beginning In June 2024
description: In June 2024, Rite Aid, the third-largest drugstore chain in the United States, experienced a cyberattack by the RansomHub ransomware group, resulting in a significant data breach. This attack compromised over 10 GB of customer information, affecting around 45 million lines of personal data, including names, addresses, driving licence ID numbers, dates of birth, and Rite Aid rewards numbers. RansomHub claimed responsibility for the attack and posted details on BreachForums, including a screenshot of some of the allegedly stolen data as proof. Rite Aid, which employs over 45,000 staff across more than 1,700 stores in 16 states, detected the breach in June and has since restored its compromised systems with the help of external cybersecurity experts. The company is currently finalising its investigation and sending notifications to affected customers. Importantly, Rite Aid confirmed that no Social Security numbers, financial information, or patient health data were impacted.
intelligence_impact: Minor data breach/exfiltration (no critical/sensitive information), data corruption (deletion/altering) and/or leaking of data

name: Unknown threat actor attacked US manufacturer Crown Equipment on 8 June 2024
description:
An unknown threat actor attacked US manufacturer Crown Equipment on 8 June 2024, the firm confirmed in an email to their employers on 20 June 2024. The email details that Crown Equipment's IT system was hacked by an "international cybercriminal organisation," which required the manufacturer to shut down its operating systems. 
The attack caused disruption at the manufacturing plants of the company and employees have been unable to clock in their hours, access service manuals, and deliver machinery in some cases, according to Bleeping Computer reporting.
intelligence_impact: No data breach/exfiltration or data corruption (deletion/altering) and/or leaking of data

name: DragonForce Group targeted servers managing 911 services in Southern Californiawith ransomware on 16 July 2024
description: According to the Californian South Bay Regional Public Communications Authority (SBRPCA), the DragonForce Group targeted servers used to manage 911 services in South California with ransomware on 16 July 2024. Among the affected cities are Manhattan Beach, Culver City, Hermosa Beach as well as El Segundo, Hawthorne and Gardena.
source_disclosure: Incident disclosed by authorities of victim state
intelligence_impact: No data breach/exfiltration or data corruption (deletion/altering) and/or leaking of data

name: BlackSuit Ransomware group hit US SaaS provider CDK Global starting 18 June 2024
description: CDK Global, a Software-as-a-Service provider for car and trucker dealers in North America, was hit by a ransomware attack on 18 June 2024 forcing it to shut down its dealer management system. The outage of the system affected roughly 15,000 car dealers in North America, who had to move back to pen and paper to continue business operations. CDK Global is reported to be negotiating with the threat actor to pay the ransom, allegedly to be in the double-digit million dollar figure.  News reporting on 22 June 2024 claimed that BlackSuit Ransomware was behind the incident.
intelligence_impact: Minor data breach/exfiltration (no critical/sensitive information), but no data corruption (deletion/altering) or leaking of data

name: BlackSuit breached the network of the Monroe County government on 1 July 2024
description: According to county officials of Monroe, they experienced an intrusion into their networks on 1 July 2024 and that the perpetrator was identified as the ransomware gang BlackSuit. The attack is still under investigation, but the extent of affected data is still unclear.
source_disclosure: Incident disclosed by authorities of victim state
intelligence_impact: No data breach/exfiltration or data corruption (deletion/altering) and/or leaking of data

name: Hacktivist group SiegedSec breached US think tank Heritage Foundation on 2 July 2024
description:
On 2 July 2024, the hacktivist group SiegedSec breached the Heritage Foundation which is a prominent conservative think tank based in Washington, D.C. On 9 July 2024, the hacker group published roughly 2 GB of the 200 GB stolen data including the full names, email addresses, passwords, and usernames of people associating with Heritage including users with U.S. government email addresses, Heritage Foundation blogs, material related to The Daily Signal. According to the hackers, they released the data in response to Heritage Foundation’s Project 2025 and to provide “transparency to the public regarding who exactly is supporting heritage”. 
In response to media inquiries, a spokesperson for the foundation claimed that the group did not compromise any networks but instead identified a public-facing archive of The Daily Signal website hosted by a contracted, which contained the data SiegedSec advertised.
intelligence_impact: Minor data breach/exfiltration (no critical/sensitive information), data corruption (deletion/altering) and/or leaking of data

name: An unknown threat actor gained unauthorized access to an Azure Sharepoint instance of Fortinet on September 2024
description: Cybersecurity giant Fortinet has confirmed it suffered a data breach after a threat actor with the moniker ‘Fortibitch’ claimed to steal 440GB of files from the company's Microsoft Sharepoint server. Fortinet is one of the largest cybersecurity companies in the world, selling secure networking products like firewalls, routers, and VPN devices. The threat actor claims to have tried to extort Fortinet into paying a ransom, likely to prevent the publishing of data, but the company refused to pay. Fortinet confirmed that customer data was stolen from a "third-party cloud-based shared file drive." Fortinet wrote in a statement on their website that there is no indication that "this incident has resulted in malicious activity affecting any customers and did not involve any data encryption, deployment of ransomware, or access to Fortinet’s corporate network." Furthermore, Fortinet’s operations, products, and services have not been impacted, and no evidence of additional access to any other Fortinet resource is found.
intelligence_impact: Data corruption (deletion/altering) but no leaking of data, no data breach/exfiltration OR major data breach / exfiltration, but no data corruption and/or leaking of data

name: The INC RANSOM ransomware gang encrypted and stole data from from US-Based Non-Profit Healthcare Provider McLaren Health Care starting on 6 August 2024
description:
​On 6 August 2024, IT and phone systems at McLaren Health Care hospitals were disrupted following an attack linked to the INC Ransom ransomware operation. McLaren hinted the hospitals had lost access to patient information databases when advising patients to bring detailed information about their current medications to appointments, including physician orders and printed results of recent lab tests. Employees at McLaren Bay Region Hospital in Bay City have shared a ransom note warning that the hospital's systems have been encrypted and stolen data will be published on INC RANSOM ransomware gang's leak site if a ransom is not paid. The incident is still under investigation.
McLaren stated that it had brought its operations fully back online by 27 August.
intelligence_impact: No data breach/exfiltration or data corruption (deletion/altering) and/or leaking of data

name: Ransomware gang Hunters International breached Omni Family Health in the United States, stealing sensitive information in August 2024
description: The Hunters International ransomware gang compromised Omni Family Health, a nonprofit organization providing healthcare services to communities in California. The group obtained personal information of nearly 470,000 current and former patients and employees in the breach. Omni Family Health discovered the intrusion on 7 August 2024, following claims that information was taken from its systems and leaked on the dark web. The data breach may have exposed varying personal information, including names, addresses, Social Security numbers, dates of birth, health insurance details, and medical information. The Hunters International ransomware gang claimed responsibility for the attack, stating they stole 2.7 terabytes of data, which was released on 23 August. The incident was officially disclosed by Omni Family Health on 19 October 2024.
intelligence_impact: Major data breach/exfiltration (critical/sensitive information) & data corruption (deletion/altering) and/or leaking of data

name: BlackSuit Ransomware group gained access to systems of the City of Killeen, Texas, on 7 August 2024
description:
According to the City of Killeen, (Texas, USA) the BlackSuit ransomware group gained access to the city's systems on Wednesday, 7 August 2024. 
The city says most of the affected systems are internal, but citizens may experience a delay in essential services at the Utility Collections division.
Upon discovery of the breach, the city took steps to secure their systems to prevent further access. As a precautionary measure, Killeen disconnected from the Bell County Network to contain the spread of the attack.
As of now, the city does not believe that personal or financial information of citizens has been exfiltrated but recommends monitoring personal bank accounts and to report any suspicious activity.
intelligence_impact: No data breach/exfiltration or data corruption (deletion/altering) and/or leaking of data

name: Qilin Ransomware group claims attack on CODAC Behavioral Healthcare (USA) on 28 August 2024
description:
The Qilin group listed CODAC Behavioral Healthcare, a non-profit health care treatment organization, as one of their latest victims on 28 August 2024. Within the stolen data are financial information, pictures of ID cards, a list of staff members—including their Social Security Numbers—and healthcare cards. 
This attack is very similar to the one on pathology lab services provider Synnovis in June 2024.
intelligence_impact: Data corruption (deletion/altering) but no leaking of data, no data breach/exfiltration OR major data breach / exfiltration, but no data corruption and/or leaking of data

name: Rhysida ransomware group target Port of Seattle and Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (USA) with Ransomware on 24 August 2024
description:
Rhysida ransomware group targeted the Port of Seattle, which also operates the Seattle-Tacoma (Sea-Tac) International Airport, with a cyberattack on 24 August 2024. The outages began early Saturday and took down several systems. While the full scale of the outage has not been made public, the Port of Seattle websites, email and phone systems were also affected. 
Security operations at Sea-Tac Airport were not impacted with 72,000 people flying out on Sunday, although the baggage sorting systems and some terminal screens at Sea-Tac Airport were disrupted. Travellers have been advised to allow extra time for their stay at the airport, use mobile applications for check-ins, and be prepared for longer-than-usual security lines and baggage claim wait times.
On 13 September, Port of Seattle confirmed that Rhysida ransomware group was behind the cyberattack. They also confirmed that Rhysida accessed and encrypted parts of their computer systems, disrupting key services like baggage handling, check-in kiosks, ticketing, Wi-Fi, and parking. Port of Seattle also stated that they refused to pay the ransom, for this reason the ransomware group may publish stolen data.
intelligence_impact: Minor data breach/exfiltration (no critical/sensitive information), but no data corruption (deletion/altering) or leaking of data

name: RansomHub stole data from the nonprofit organization Planned Parenthood in late August 2024
description: In late August, Planned Parenthood suffered a cyberattack causing a disruption and sensitive data may be stolen. Planned Parenthood is a non-profit organization that provides sexual health care services. It is not yet known whether any personal information about patients might have been stolen, but that could potentially be devastating. The group behind the attack, Ransomhub, has claimed responsibility on their leak site. The listing on the leak site shows financial information, court papers, and insurance certificates.
intelligence_impact: Data corruption (deletion/altering) but no leaking of data, no data breach/exfiltration OR major data breach / exfiltration, but no data corruption and/or leaking of data

name: Ransomware gang Nitrogen gained access to network of SRP Federal Credit Union USA, beginning on September 5, 2024
description: Between September 5, 2024, and November 4, 2024, Unknown Threat Actors, later identified as Nitrogen ransomware gang, breached the confidentiality of SRP Federal Credit Union systems, potentially acquiring files containing sensitive information, including names, Social Security numbers, drivers license numbers, dates of birth, and financial information, impacting approximately 240,000 individuals. SRP Federal Credit Union, detected the incident and law enforcement was notified, leading to an investigation that concluded on November 22, 2024. Nitrogen ransomware gang claimed responsibility for the attack on December 5, 2024, stating they had stolen 650 GB of customer data.
intelligence_impact: Data corruption (deletion/altering) but no leaking of data, no data breach/exfiltration OR major data breach / exfiltration, but no data corruption and/or leaking of data

name: The BianLian Ransomware Group Gained Access to Boston Children's Health Physicians (BCHP) and Stole Certain Files Beginning at Least on 10 September 2024
description:
The BianLian ransomware group claimed on 16 October 2024, that it gained access to Boston Children's Health Physicians (BCHP) and stole certain files starting at least on 10 September 2024.
The BCHP incident notification stated that an unnamed BCHP IT provider detected suspicious activity on its network and subsequently informed the BCHP on 6 September 2024. On 10 September 2024, the BCHP also discovered unauthorized activity in limited portions of the network. Working with an IT security firm, the unauthorized access on 10 September 2024, was confirmed, as was the extraction of certain files.
The stolen files included current and former employee, patient, and guarantor information such as names, Social Security numbers, addresses, dates of birth, driver's license numbers, medical record numbers, health insurance information, billing information, and/or limited treatment information.

name: RansomHub ransomware gang hacked HCF Management in the United States between 17 September 2024 and 3 October 2024
description: On 17 September 2024, the ransomware gang RansomHub gained unauthorized access to HCF Management's computer systems. The breach affected nearly 70,000 people. Heritage Health Care reported the largest breach, affecting 12,162 people. Hempfield Manor was the single facility with the most patients reported affected, at 4,744. RansomHub added HCF to its dark web site on 29 October 2024, and claimed to have published 250 Gbytes of HCF's data. HCF learned of the breach on 3 October 2024, and engaged an external computer forensic firm to assist. The investigation found that threat actors accessed and acquired documents from the company's IT systems between 17 September 2024 and 3 October 2024, potentially including residents' names, addresses, phone numbers, date of birth, Social Security numbers, medical treatment information, and health insurance information. HCF reported the breach to federal and state regulators on 9 January 2025.
intelligence_impact: Not available

name: Interlock ransomware stole sensitive data of 1.4 million patients from Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center in the USA beginning on September 17, 2024
description: Interlock ransomware group, breached the Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center and its El Paso counterpart in September 2024, potentially exposing the data of 1.4 million patients, including full name, date of birth, physical address, Social Security number, driver's license number, government ID number, financial account information, health insurance information, medical information, billing/claims data, diagnosis and treatment information, by disrupting computer systems and applications, and stealing sensitive data between September 17 and September 29, 2024, with the incident being reported to the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office for Civil Rights and disclosed to the public on December 16, 2024, and the attackers leaking 2.1 million files totalling 2.6 TB of data on the dark web on October 27, 2024.
intelligence_impact: Major data breach/exfiltration (critical/sensitive information) & data corruption (deletion/altering) and/or leaking of data

name: RansomHub ransomware gang stole personal and health information of US BayMark Health Services between September and October 2024
description: Unknown Threat Actors breached the IT systems of BayMark Health Services, the largest US addiction treatment provider, between September 24, 2024, and October 14, 2024, stealing personal and health information of an undisclosed number of patients, including names, Social Security numbers, driver's license numbers, dates of birth, services received, insurance information, and treatment and diagnostic information. The breach was discovered on October 11, 2024, following an IT systems disruption, and was claimed by the RansomHub ransomware gang, which uploaded 1.5TB of stolen files on its dark web leak site. BayMark Health Services notified the affected patients starting January 8, 2025 and offered them a year of free Equifax identity monitoring services.
intelligence_impact: Not available

name: Stormous Ransomware Group Stole Sensitive Data from Crypto Payment Service Transak in October 2024
description: In October 2024, Stormous ransomware group compromised the Transak company, which provides an 'onamp' service for many famous blockchain companies, by exploiting a data leak caused by employees using laptops for non-work purposes, affecting some 93,000 unique users, including passports, ID cards, and personal photos, and is now trying to negotiate with the company, demanding $30,000 to remove the stolen data, which includes classified private documents, government identifications, addresses, financial statements, and personal photos of users, with the company classifying the damage as 'low or moderate' due to the lack of sensitive information such as social security numbers and credit card details, and the CEO, Sami Stairt, stating that the company is not interested in negotiating with the ransomware group.
intelligence_impact: Minor data breach/exfiltration (no critical/sensitive information), but no data corruption (deletion/altering) or leaking of data

name: IntelBroker, Together with Hacking Groups EnergyWeaponUser and zjj, Breached the Systems of Cisco on 6 October 2024 and Exfiltrated Customer Data
description:
Unknown threat actors, allegedly IntelBroker, EnergyWeaponUser and zjj, breached the systems of Cisco, a networking hardware and software manufacturer, on 6 October 2024, and exfiltrated data belonging to it and its customers, including Github projects, Gitlab Projects, SonarQube projects, source code, hard-coded credentials, certificates, customer SRCs, Cisco confidential documents, Jira tickets, API tokens, AWS Private buckets, Cisco Technology SRCs, Docker Builds, Azure Storage buckets, Private & Public keys, SSL Certificates, and Cisco Premium Products, as well as the production source code of a large number of organisations, including Vodafone Australia, National Australia Bank (NAB) and Microsoft, according to claims posted by IntelBroker on a popular dark web hacking forum, which Cisco has acknowledged and is currently investigating. The attackers gained access to a DevHub environment, which was publicly accessible and contained software code and scripts, among other things, for customers. The instance has since been taken offline. Cisco has confirmed that data was leaked that was not intended for public download, but states that this does not include any financial data. The investigation is still ongoing, and the network equipment provider states that it is proactively approaching affected customers.
On 16 December 2024, IntelBroker leaked 2.9 GB of data belonging to Cisco on the Breach Forums platform. The leaked data included sensitive information from Cisco products and services, such as Cisco ISE (Identity Services Engine), Cisco SASE (Secure Access Service Edge), Cisco Webex, Cisco Umbrella, Cisco IOS XE & XR, and a Wireless LAN Controller software image. IntelBroker claimed this partial leak was intended to prove the legitimacy of the breach to potential buyers. The fate of the remaining 4.5 TB of data remains uncertain.
intelligence_impact: Major data breach/exfiltration (critical/sensitive information) & data corruption (deletion/altering) and/or leaking of data

name: RansomHub Gang Breached The US-City Of Coppell, Texas On 23 October 2024
description: On 23 October 2024, the RansomHub gang breached the confidentiality and availability of the information systems of the City of Coppell, Texas with a ransomware attack. The City of Coppell reported widespread technology issues, including an internet outage, unavailable WiFi at city facilities, and disruptions to library services, permitting and inspection platforms, and the municipal court. The City of Coppell announced the attack on 23 October 2024 and by the RansomHub gang on 25 November 2024. The City Manager of the City of Coppell, Mike Land, informed the public about the attack and its potential impact on the data of individuals and vendors. The City of Coppell restored some of its operations by 1, 15 and 20 November 2024.
intelligence_impact: Minor data breach/exfiltration (no critical/sensitive information), data corruption (deletion/altering) and/or leaking of data

name: The hacker known as abyss0 allegedly stole a large amount of presumably customer data from financial technology company Finastra
description: On 7 November 2024, Finastra detected suspicious activity on its internally hosted file transfer platform, which led to the discovery of a large-scale data breach. Using the nickname 'abyss0', an unknown threat actor had stolen over 400 gigabytes of data, including customer information, and began selling it on the cybercrime community BreachForums on 8 November 2024. This actor also tried to sell the stolen data before, on 31 October 2024. Therefore, the breach is believed to have occurred at least a week before detection, with the threat actor gaining access to Finastra's file-sharing system through compromised credentials. Finastra notified its customers, including 45 of the world's top 50 banks, and implemented an alternative secure file-sharing platform to ensure continuity. The company is still investigating the root cause and scope of the breach and has been sharing Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) and updates with its customers. KrebsOnSecurity reported the incident on 19 November 2024.
intelligence_impact: Minor data breach/exfiltration (no critical/sensitive information), but no data corruption (deletion/altering) or leaking of data

name: Embargo Ransomware Gang launched a ransomware attack on Memorial Hospital and Manor in the United States on 2 November 2024
description:
Embargo Ransomware Gang launched a ransomware attack on Memorial Hospital and Manor, an 80-bed hospital in Bainbridge, Georgia, on 2 November 2024, disrupting the hospital's Electronic Health Records (EHR) system, which was discovered early Saturday morning when employees saw notifications of potential risks found by the virus protection software, and the hospital has since reverted to paper-based processes while evaluating options to restore and recover its EHR, as disclosed by the hospital in a statement on Facebook on 3 November 2024.
The Embargo ransomware gang claimed responsibility for this ransomware attack on November 5, 2024 and also claimed to have stolen 1.15 TB of data.
intelligence_impact: No data breach/exfiltration or data corruption (deletion/altering) and/or leaking of data

name: Intel Broker leaked personal data of 290,762 individuals from MIT Technology Review Magazine in the United States via a third-party contractor on 4 November 2024
description: The hacker known as Intel Broker breached MIT Technology Review Magazine via a third-party contractor, leaking nearly 300,000 user records on Breach Forums on 4 November 2024. The data includes full names, email addresses, and activity details, posing risks for phishing and targeted scams. Intel Broker, notorious for recent attacks on high-profile organizations, alleges that the data includes Personally Identifiable Information. Hackread.com analyzed the leaked data and can confirm it includes personal details, which, while not as sensitive as financial data, could be leveraged in phishing attempts or targeted scams. The leak does not appear to contain highly sensitive information like social security numbers or financial data, but the compromised data is still a privacy risk, as it could be exploited for phishing scams or identity verification attacks. MIT Technology Review, an esteemed publication from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is known for its analysis of emerging technologies and their impact on society. This data breach potentially exposes readers and contributors who engaged with the platform, a situation that may lead to reputational challenges for the publication, as well as privacy concerns for its user base. Hackread.com disclosed the attack on 4 November 2024.
intelligence_impact: Minor data breach/exfiltration (no critical/sensitive information), data corruption (deletion/altering) and/or leaking of data

name: The Termite ransomware group disrupted the managed services hosted environment of supply chain management and software provider Blue Yonder since at least 21 November 2024
description:
The Termite ransomware group disrupted the managed services hosted environment of supply chain management and software provider Blue Yonder since at least 21 November 2024, Blue Yonder reported in an incident notification for the first time on 22 November 2024.
The incident involved a ransomware attack, and at least at the coffee chain Starbucks, the incident disrupted the system they use to track and manage their employees' schedules. The retailer Wm Morrison Supermarkets was also affected. In December 2024, the Termite ransomware group claimed to have exfiltrated 680 GB of data, including databases, email lists "for future attacks" (over 16,000 entries), miscellaneous documents (over 200,000), reports, and insurance documents.
On January 29, 2025, Morrisons supermarkets reported that the cyberattack on its technology supplier, Blue Yonder, in November disrupted product availability and impacted Christmas sales. CEO Rami Baitieh explained that the attack forced the shutdown of the company’s warehouse management system, resulting in a temporary loss of visibility over fresh produce and fruit and vegetable stock levels.
intelligence_impact: Minor data breach/exfiltration (no critical/sensitive information), but no data corruption (deletion/altering) or leaking of data

name: Black Basta Ransomware Gang Breached Mortgage Investors Group in the USA Using Ransomware Between 11 December 2024 and 12 December 2024
description: Mortgage Investors Group (MIG), a Tennessee-based mortgage lender, was breached by the Black Basta Ransomware Gang in a cyberattack that started on 11 December 2024 and was discovered on 12 December 2024, resulting in the exposure of sensitive personal information, including full names and financial information, of an undisclosed number of customers. The company hired a vendor to identify affected individuals and notify them directly in several weeks.
intelligence_impact: Not available

name: IntelBroker Stole Documents from US-American Information Technology Company Hewlett Packard Enterprise Using API, WePay, and GitHub Repositories Breach on 16 January 2025
description: On 16 January 2025, the US-American multinational information technology company Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) was informed by IntelBroker that they had stolen documents from HPE's developer environments, including source code, certificates, and personal information. IntelBroker claimed to have had access to HPE's API, WePay, and GitHub repositories for at least two days. HPE immediately launched an investigation and activated their cyber response protocols. As of 20 January 2025, HPE had not found any evidence of a security breach. The incident was reported by BleepingComputer, who was informed by HPE spokesperson Clare Loxley. IntelBroker announced the sale of the allegedly stolen information on Breach Forums, a cybercrime and data breach forum, and also shared details with Hackread.com. description: On 8 February 2025, Medusa Ransomware Group claimed to have breached SimonMed Imaging, a US-based diagnostic imaging company, stealing over 212 GB of sensitive data and exposing private information of more than 132,000 individuals, including patients and employees, before demanding a $1 million ransom in Bitcoin. The group posted 45 proof files online. A company representative said the breach occurred last week, but SimonMed “interrupted” hackers and “no data was encrypted.” Clinical systems were not impacted by this “unauthorized activity". Furthermore, "to immediately contain the situation, we temporarily took some systems offline, resulting in some operational slowdowns.”

name: Unknown threat actors hacked  crypto-focused Infini Neobank on 24 February 2025 stealing USD Coins worth $49.5 million
description: On 24 February 2025, Infini Neobank was hacked, resulting in the theft of $49.5 million USDC, which was then transferred to the Ethereum network. The attacker traded the stolen USDC for Ethereum-based DAI and purchased 17.696 ETH, later transferring it to the address 0xfcc8...6e49. The attack was likely carried out by obtaining a private key, with the private key to the address 0xc49b...e3e1 possibly being leaked. The stolen assets were transferred to wallets associated with TornadoCash, an anonymization protocol. An Infini developer, who secretly retained executive authority after the project was completed, is thought to be behind the attack. An official police report has been filed, and a member of Infini's team claimed that the engineer who committed the theft had been identified and reported to the police.

name: Unknown threat actor dubbed Codefinger encrypt S3 buckets in Amazon Web Services using ServerSide Encryption with Customer Provided Keys at least until January 2025

Codefinger used compromised AWS credentials to locate victims' keys, generated an encryption key locally to encrypt the targets' data, and set a seven-day file deletion policy using the S3 Object Lifecycle Management API. Ransom notes were dropped on all affected directories, instructing the victim to pay ransom on a given Bitcoin address in exchange for the custom AES256 key, with a warning that any attempt to change account permissions or modify files on the bucket would result in the termination of negotiations, leaving the victim with no way to recover their data.

name: Venezuelan National Electoral Council allegedly targeted with DDoS after the presidential election on 28 July 2024
description:
According to President Maduro, the Venezuelan National Electoral Council was allegedly targeted with DDoS after the Presidential election on 28 July 2024, which he stated as the reason for why the authorities have not released detailed vote counts at that time. Furthermore, he blamed Elon Musk for the attack and argued that the election system has been hacked as part of a plot against him. However, the hacking collective Anonymous also claimed the hack for itself.
There have been no external verifications of the DDoS operation, but the Venezuelan state airline Conviasa was also disrupted a few days later. The US network security provider Netscout reported on 31 July of an observed tenfold increase in DDoS attacks against Venezuelan websites on July 29.
On 14 August, the Chilean hacker Astra gave an interview to the medium Publimetro and claimed responsibility for the cyber incident on what was supposed to be the National Electoral Council. In the interview, Astra, also the leader of the hacker group Cyber Hunters, explained that they had discovered an unsecured ghost machine used to rig the elections. Astra said that they blocked this ghost machine from accessing the electoral system and stole the database it contained, with entries for 19 million residents, many of whom were already deceased. Astra also announced that the cyber incidents against Maduro will become more frequent and automated.

name: Dark Pink APT targeted state and corporate organizations in the Asia-Pacific and Europe since mid-2021
description:
In an eponymous cyber-operation, a newly-discovered APT group named Dark Pink was observed by Group-IB Global to have launched a series of successful malware and spearphishing campaigns against government, military, and corporate entities predominantly based in the Asia-Pacific (APAC) region. Initial attacks date back to at least June 2022, with some indications that the group may have been active as early as May 2021. 
The group likely operates out of the APAC region. Group-IB analysis acknowledges earlier reporting by Chinese cybersecurity researchers at the Anheng Information Shadows Hunting Lab from early January 2023, which tracked overlapping TTPs in a similar target space under the label Saaiwc Group. According to Singapore-headquartered Group-IB Global, which split from its Russia-based parent company in July 2022 to maintain international business accounts in light of sanctions against Russia and the company itself, Dark Pink's objectives are primarily corporate espionage and data theft.
The APT group Dark Pink has been attacking various state and non-state targets in Europe and Asia since February 2022. An update to a report by the cyber security company Group-IB, which for the first time publicly disclosed the new threat actor in January 2023, reveals new details of the sophisticated operations conducted by the group. Although the dutch cyber security company EclecticIQ attributes the group with low confidence to China, the Group-IB does not connect the group to any state actors. Among the newly identified targets is an educational institution in Belgium, a military body in Thailand and government targets in Brunei and Indonesia.

name: Criminal threat actor XE Group exploited Progress Telerik vulnerability to infiltrate a US government agency alongside other threat actors beginning in August 2021
description:
According to the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), several groups, including the criminal threat actor XE Group, breached a federal civilian executive branch (FCEB) agency between November 2022 and January 2023. Attackers gained access via an unpatched Microsoft Internet Information Services (IIS) web server by exploiting a known critical vulnerability (CVE-2019-18935) in Progress Telerik's user interface (UI) software, which facilitates remote code execution.
Besides XE Group, CISA linked active exploitation to an unnamed APT. In a report from 7 December 2021, Volexity identified XE Group as a collective of cybercriminals originating from Vietnam. No further details have been revealed about the additional threat actors or their motives. 
Based on CISA's assessment, the affected agency’s vulnerability scanner was equipped to detect CVE-2019-18935 but failed to alert about the vulnerability because the Telerik software was installed in a file path the scanner was not configured to read. No patch is currently available for older versions of Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX (builds before R1 2020), which remain vulnerable. In 2020, the NSA had listed the four-year-old vulnerability among the top 25 software flaws for which it tracked active abuse by Chinese state-sponsored hackers.

name: A Yemeni Houthi-aligned hacker group infected the cell phones of military personnel in various Middle Eastern countries with the GuardZoo malware beginning in October 2019
description:
A Yemeni Houthi-aligned hacker group infected the cell phones of military personnel in various Middle Eastern countries with the GuardZoo malware beginning in October 2019, the US IT security firm Lookout reported in a report on 9 July 2024.
The report stated that the hacker group enticed end users to install the GuardZoo surveillanceware, a variant of the Dendroid RAT spyware leaked in 2014, on their devices. They used military and religious themes to trick users into downloading the software through WhatsApp, WhatsApp Business, or as a downloadable file in a web browser.
The military personnel most affected were those in Yemen, particularly the members of the pro-Hadi forces under the internationally recognized government. Additionally, military personnel in Saudi Arabia and Egypt were also affected. Those in Oman, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Turkey were less affected.
